events.continuity_hook: This follows the first Santa Fe anniversary planning pass once the PTO answer makes the Thursday departure realistic.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the dates, airport plan, flights, hotel, rental-car need, seat requests, and any booking holds before the better rooms disappear.
events.scenario_brief: Erin’s spouse gets Friday PTO approved, so the anniversary weekend locks to Thursday through Sunday instead of the Friday-through-Monday fallback. The Thursday afternoon Denver-to-Santa Fe nonstop is still available but priced above the Albuquerque alternatives, while Albuquerque would save money at the cost of an evening rental-car drive and a later first-night arrival. The downtown boutique inn can hold a balcony king but has no pool or hot tub, the resort outside the center has pool, hot tub, fitness access, and easy parking, and the plaza-area hotel is convenient but valet costs make it less attractive. The unresolved choice is whether to pay for the simpler Santa Fe flights and which hotel style best fits a recovery-focused weekend.

events.continuity_hook: This is the final practical pass after Erin chose the simpler Santa Fe flight plan and the resort-style stay.
events.interaction_goal: Organize airport timing, rental pickup, hotel arrival, dinner timing, packing for temperature swings, seat monitoring, and the short weekend itinerary without over-scheduling the trip.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before departure, Erin and her spouse have booked the Thursday afternoon Denver-to-Santa Fe nonstop, the Sunday late-morning return, the resort outside the center, and a compact rental car. The resort confirms parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness access, but the balcony-style patio request is noted rather than guaranteed. Late-September weather could swing from warm afternoons to chilly evenings, the anniversary dinner time still needs to be matched against sunset, and the return seat map has changed since booking.

events.continuity_hook: This begins the next certification-style work trip after the anniversary travel is off Erin’s calendar.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked plan for arrival day, return timing, hotel area, event-block deadline, rideshare versus rental car, and the schedule questions Erin should confirm before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Santa Fe weekend, Erin is assigned to a mid-October instructor certification lab in Nashville. The formal sessions run Tuesday through Thursday near Vanderbilt, with a possible Monday afternoon calibration and a Thursday evening trainer dinner still pending. A Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Nashville nonstop gives the calmest start, a Monday morning arrival saves one hotel night but becomes risky if calibration is required, and Saturday arrival feels unnecessary. Hotel options include the official block closest to the lab with a high rate and limited amenities, a Midtown suite hotel with strong reviews, pool, and fitness access but no listed hot tub, and a quieter West End hotel with better room comfort but a longer rideshare. Local transportation is still unsettled because she may not need a rental car if the week stays centered near the lab.

events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Nashville plan after the lab schedule and Monday calibration requirement become firm.
events.interaction_goal: Choose and prepare to book the outbound and return flights, hotel, local transportation plan, room request, seat selections, and expense notes.
events.scenario_brief: The Nashville coordinator confirms that Monday calibration is required at 3:00 p.m., the Thursday classroom portion should end by 2:30 p.m., and the trainer dinner is optional rather than required. That makes the Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Nashville nonstop the safest outbound, while the Monday morning arrival is no longer worth the risk. The Midtown suite hotel can hold a quiet king room and has pool and fitness access, the official block is still closer but more expensive with fewer recovery amenities, and the West End hotel is attractive but adds more daily rideshare time. The remaining decision is whether to book a Thursday evening return after the final session or add a Friday morning return for a less rushed pack-up.

events.continuity_hook: This is a narrow post-booking change after the Nashville assessment schedule shifts later on the final day.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to move to the Friday morning nonstop, then outline the flight change, extra hotel night, expense note, and coordinator notification steps.
events.scenario_brief: After Erin books the Sunday afternoon nonstop, the Midtown suite hotel through Thursday checkout, rideshare-only local transportation, and a Thursday evening return, the certifying group moves her practical scoring slot to late Thursday afternoon and asks instructors to turn in equipment by 5:30 p.m. The booked return is now too tight once pack-up, rideshare timing, bag drop, and security are included. A late Thursday one-stop is available but would get her home after midnight, while a Friday morning nonstop is cleaner and the hotel can extend one night at the same rate if her expense approval covers it.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Nashville planning after the late Thursday scoring slot pushed Erin to the calmer Friday return.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final logistics pass for airport timing, rideshares, rain packing, training-kit backup items, hotel arrival, assessment-day pack-up, return seat selection, and the Friday checkout plan.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before leaving for Nashville, Erin has changed to the Friday morning return, extended the Midtown suite hotel by one night, and kept the no-rental plan. The hotel confirms the quiet-room request plus pool and fitness access, but the hot tub is unavailable. Rain is likely during the week, the lab has received her shipped training kit, and she still wants a compact carry-on backup in case any materials are delayed. The outbound window seat is set, while the Friday return seat map has shifted after an aircraft swap.
